title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Pole
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：dragon　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dragon 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my grandfather ① carved a dragon that no neighbour in the town would have carried, and he said the carving was the whole of the winter. The ② dragon, meaning the figure and not the tyrant, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a dragon, he said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left uncarried.

Every ③ dragon in that town had the same short pole at the end of it, and the ④ dragon at the end, meaning the one they kept for the lantern night and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A dragon, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to carry; my grandfather said the carrying is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dragon was the whole of the story, meaning the tyrant and not the figure. The ⑥ dragon, meaning the tyrant and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody fears and nobody reasons with; dragon, he said, is either something you carve or the only word that means both a figure and a tyrant. He said the tyrant is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ dragon had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short pole. The ⑧ dragon of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in January, was one town and fourteen winters of carrying; dragon, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to carry. She said the carrying was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dragon I remember is the one named in the list, which burnt in 1970 and is still described as the quietest in the town. A ⑩ dragon, my grandmother said in 1972, is the only one that improves by being carried; every dragon, she said, is a tyrant that has agreed to look like a figure. She said the tyrant was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 龙（指那个镇子上舞着的那一条）
B. n. 龙（指那条龙形本身，与凶悍的人相对）
C. 固定搭配：carve a dragon 雕一条龙
D. n. 龙（指留给灯会用的那一条）
E. n. 龙（抽象总称，指一个镇子的舞龙之事）
F. n. 龙（指名录上写到、被列名的那一条）
G. n. 凶悍的人；悍妇（指故事里人人怕却无人敢与之讲理的那个人）
H. n. 凶悍的人（抽象总称，指人人怕却无人敢与之讲理的那种人）

items.q: carved a dragon that no neighbour in the town would have carried
The dragon, meaning the figure and not the tyrant

answers.why: carve a dragon 意为“雕一条龙”，1949 年祖父雕了一条镇子上没有一位邻居肯去举的龙。
dragon 意为“龙”，指那条龙形本身而不是凶悍的人，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
dragon 意为“龙”，指那个镇子上的每一条龙，每一条到头都有同一根短短的撑杆。
dragon 意为“龙”，指留给灯会用的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
dragon 意为“凶悍的人、悍妇”，指故事里人人怕却无人敢与之讲理的那个人，叔叔说这个悍人就是那个故事的全部。
dragon 意为“凶悍的人”，指人人怕却无人敢与之讲理的那种人而不是那条龙形，是故事里人人都怕、却无人敢与之讲理的东西。
dragon 意为“龙”，指名录上写到、被列名的那一条，到 1958 年这条龙成了名录里的一行。
dragon 意为“龙”，祖父一月写道，整件事的舞龙之事是一个镇子和十四个冬天的举龙。
dragon 意为“龙”，我记得的是名录上列名的那一条，1970 年被烧掉了，至今仍被说成镇子上最安静的一条。
dragon 为抽象总称，祖母 1972 年说，一条龙是唯一会因为被好好举着而变得更好的东西。
